open_points.subject: omitted imported project name and alias
open_points.text: “each with the display name and alias it arrives under” conflicts with A16’s “its v1 name and no alias unless the owner gives others”
open_points.question: When a mapping request picks a project but omits a replacement display name or alias, does this operation apply the v1-name/no-alias defaults, or report missing inputs and keep the mapping unclean?
options: Use the v1 display name and no alias by default
Require the request to supply the resolved display name and alias explicitly
Default only the alias, while treating an omitted display name as missing
open_points.default_guess: Use the v1 display name and no alias unless the owner explicitly supplies replacements.

witness.initial: An accepted export contains project P with v1 display name “Casa” and no alias.
events: The owner selects P without entering a replacement display name or alias.
operations calls read_import_mapping in mapping mode.
outcomes: The operation resolves P to display name “Casa”, no alias, and the mapping can be clean.
The operation reports the display name as missing because every pick was required to carry its arrival name, so no confirmation step can be shown.
witness.observer: The owner, who either can or cannot proceed to confirmation.

open_points.subject: upload projection of an out-of-vocabulary project status
open_points.text: “At `upload`, each project the file holds with its id and status” while “a status outside its vocabulary is not [file_malformed], but a malformed record of a pick”
open_points.question: How does the upload-mode output represent a readable project status that is outside the project-status vocabulary, given that upload must not reject it as `file_malformed`?
options: Return the project with a separate invalid-status marker
Omit or replace the invalid status in the upload projection
open_points.default_guess: Return the raw status text together with an explicit validity indication so the project remains selectable and can later be reported malformed.

witness.initial: An export parses successfully and contains project P with id P and status `paused`.
events: operations calls read_import_mapping in upload mode.
outcomes: The upload answer lists P with the raw status `paused`.
The upload answer lists P with an invalid-status marker or substituted status because its status field admits only the closed vocabulary.
witness.observer: The owner interface rendering the upload result.

open_points.subject: identity of malformed records
open_points.text: “Each malformed record is named by its kind and id ...; an id that occurs twice names every record that carries it”
open_points.question: How is a malformed room or pointer identified when its id is missing, and how are two records with the same kind and id distinguished so that every offending record can be named?
options: Use a source-record position or path in addition to kind and optional id
Use kind with a nullable id and collapse duplicate records into one diagnostic
Treat an unidentifiable record as a file-level refusal instead of a mapping defect
open_points.default_guess: Include a stable source-record position or path, plus kind and the id when present.

witness.initial: A picked project contains one room with no `room_id` and two pointer records carrying the same pointer id.
events: The owner requests the mapping for that project.
read_import_mapping detects all three rule-4 defects.
outcomes: The mapping identifies the records by source positions, with the room id absent and separate entries for both pointers.
The mapping reports one `room` with a null id and one duplicate-pointer diagnostic keyed only by the shared id, so the individual source records are not identified.
witness.observer: The owner correcting the export and any code that binds diagnostics to source records.

open_points.subject: validation of imported Customer kind
open_points.text: “for each Customer ... its name, its kind” and “names read with `given_values` (A02)” do not say how an out-of-vocabulary Customer kind is answered
open_points.question: If a supplied Customer kind is present but is neither `person` nor `company`, does the operation refuse the mapping request with `outside_closed_list`, return an unclean mapping with a missing/invalid value, or allow it until confirmation?
options: Return the mapping as unclean with an invalid Customer-kind item
Accept it here and reject it at confirmation
open_points.default_guess: Refuse it at stage (4) as `invalid_request` with `outside_closed_list`.

witness.initial: A picked project uses v1 customer value C.
events: The owner supplies C’s name and kind `association`.
operations calls read_import_mapping in mapping mode.
outcomes: The operation returns a mapping, marking C invalid or missing and `clean: false`.
witness.observer: The owner interface, which either renders a request refusal or a correctable mapping.

open_points.subject: identity of production-id conflicts
open_points.text: “every id of a record the picks bring in that production already holds” together with “Ids are unique per kind”
open_points.question: Does each conflict identify the record kind and the particular imported record, or does the mapping return only the conflicting identifier value?
options: Return kind, id, and the imported record’s location
Return only id values, preserving duplicates
Return a deduplicated set of id values
open_points.default_guess: Return the record kind, id, and imported-record location for every conflict.

witness.initial: Production has a Room with UUID X and a Pointer with UUID X; this is allowed because uniqueness is per kind. A picked project also brings a Room X and Pointer X.
events: The owner requests the mapping for the picked project.
read_import_mapping compares imported ids with production per kind.
outcomes: The mapping reports two distinct conflicts: room X and pointer X.
The mapping reports only X, possibly once, leaving the conflicting kinds indistinguishable.
witness.observer: The owner deciding which source records must be corrected.
